hosting.//1: cleanUrls makes /dashboard serve dashboard.html. This replaced a catch-all rewrite of ** -> /index.html, which was wrong for a Next.js static export: `output: export` emits a real HTML file per route (dashboard.html, history.html, reports.html, reports/detail.html), and the rewrite intercepted every request before extension resolution, so ALL deep links served the home page. Client-side navigation hid it - the Next router rendered the right page once loaded - but a hard refresh, a bookmark, or a shared link landed on the chat page. Unmatched paths now fall through to the exported 404.html.
hosting.//2: Order matters: Firebase applies the LAST matching rule for a given header key, so the broad rule comes first and the specific override comes after. Verified empirically - with the catch-all placed second, it clobbered the immutable rule for _next/static.

headers.//: Default for HTML pages and RSC .txt payloads, which are NOT content-hashed: the same URL must serve new bytes after a deploy. Firebase's default of max-age=3600 meant a deploy stayed invisible at the CDN edge for up to an hour, with stale HTML still pointing at the previous build's chunks. no-cache still stores the response but revalidates against the ETag first, so a deploy is visible immediately and an unchanged page costs only a 304. This must be a catch-all: header globs match the REQUEST path, and a clean route like /dashboard has no .html extension to match on.
Override for build assets. Next.js content-hashes everything under _next/static, so a given URL's bytes never change - cache for a year and skip revalidation entirely.
